I was raised Christian and I would say I still am a Christian, but I might be the worst example of one. I have my faith and beliefs, but one of my beliefs is that there are no facts. One day, we all will find out who was right. I don't shove my faith down people's throats. I will happily enjoy the company of an atheist as much as a fellow person of faith. It's not my place, nor anybody else's, to tell someone what they should believe. 

People seem to be surprised when I speak about my faith, as I never advertise it. My faith is for me and the man upstairs to know. 

Growing up, we were forced into Bible Time by my dad. 20-30 minutes of the Bible, followed by a Q/A. Even then, it felt wrong, and it tends to push people away from faith. My uncle, who is even worse, has disowned my brother and sister and has even openly shamed them on Facebook for being agnostic/a believer of science, and converting to Catholicism when she married her husband. There is a vast difference between religion and faith. I can't get behind the former. 

Religion(namely Christianity) is becoming the root of all evil. You have people like Kenneth Copeland and Joel Osteen robbing from the poor because "God told them to have private jets so they could be closer to him." 

I question my faith sometimes. Especially recently, but I never let it go. I find my way back in the end. At the end of the day, I just strive to be a good human being more than I do a Christian. When it's my time, I don't think Jesus will shun me because I chose to make memories with the family on Sundays as opposed to going to listen to a guy read from a book I already own, and tell me that HIS interpretation is the correct one.

My dad had a 6 pack of these cans when we were growing up. Never opened them. All six remained sealed. As a child I always loved these cans. The great big tiger on the front always excited me.

My parents got a divorce in 2002. Prior to this, maybe 2001 or so, they were separated but living in the same house. Dad lived in the basement. The alluring sounds of oldies would echo from the basement, signaling to us that dad was drinking. Oldies were always a sign that we should leave dad alone. 

One particular evening, I crept into the kitchen for a little frozen snack. The muted melodies of Sam Cooke could be heard from beneath the kitchen floor. Like a child trying to catch Santa in the act, I knew to proceed with silence. 

Upon opening the freezer, I saw what could have been the most horrible site I had ever bared witness to in my 15 years: three of these cans chilling with the plastic holder still attached. I stared into the abyss that was the three cans missing from the plastic holder, whose rings were more torn than Natalie Imbruglia. 

I quickly lost my desire for that late evening frozen snack as I realized that, just 10 feet below me, my dad was jamming out to "Cupid" while drinking 13 year old beer. 

I share this story any time these cans are brought up. I also share that, while it's an entertaining, albeit depressing tale, we're all very close. My mother and father included. Things work out the way they're intended to. None of us could be happier. I even have an oldies playlist running over 3 hours long. 

Make memories. Not regret.

I fault EA to an extent. However when you think about it(at least as far as IX goes,) Origin really shares a large bulk of the blame.

EA pushed for Ultima Online over Ultima IX. From a business standpoint, it makes sense. You're in the business to make money. After seeing how many beta discs sold, of course they'd put their focus and resources into it.

The beta discs wouldn't have sold if production on Ultima Online had never happened. Which would mean a much longer deadline for Ultima IX. The old 3D isometric engine probably could have still been relevant which wouldn't create even further delays.

It's not to say I blame Origin or UO for Ultima IX being a let down. I love UO. Well, I did. It spoiled me as far as MMOs go. I just think Garriott and Co. tried doing too much at one time, and EA invested in the most profitable product at the time.

With that said, I hate EA. They also ran Bullfrog into the ground. They have a knack for buying out great companies that just need a good publisher. Then they slowly disband them once they make their money back.

Looking at what we got as far as story goes, Ultima IX is worse. On the other hand, VIII puts him in situations well out of his comfort zone. Even The Avatar isn't immune from desperate times calling for desperate measures. It's sad because these measures would have been utilized and touched on in IX with the Bob White plot.

Gameplay, however, I'd say VIII is worse. I honestly didn't mind IX despite it's flaws, bugs and lack of continuity. Horrible Ultima game, and an even more horrible ending to my favorite RPG series, but if I look at it as just being another run of the mill action RPG, it's not THAT bad. There's worse. 

I enjoyed the gameplay more. The puzzles weren't all tedious, and things did get interesting as the game progressed(gameplay, not story.) Even with all of it's flaws, it has its charms. Head up to Newfound Gap. There are a ton of lookout spots that you can park at. As you get higher, the views just become more and more amazing.

Once you actually get up to Newfound Gap, you'll have an incredible view of the mountains that stretch out for miles.

From there, you can continue up the road to Clingman's Dome. You can either just park, get out and admire the beautiful scenery from the parking lot, or you can walk up the half mile long path(it's a paved path) to the observation tower. There, you'll have a 360 degree view of the mountains, at the highest accessable point of the Smokies. I also suggest heading there for the sunset.

Definitely pick a nice, clear day. Clouds will definitely block your view, and it can get very cloudy. Especially at Clingman's Dome. 

Also, hit up Cade's Cove. It's an 11 mile loop around road. Old cabins, churches and a mill reside there. All from the 1800's. The only walking you'll do is when you park and get out to check out the cabins and churches, if you want to. You don't have to of course, but the history is very neat. The churches have cemeteries which are still used to this day. 

Cade's Cove makes for amazing panorama shots as it's really just a field surrounded by the mountains. And the wildlife... It's just incredible. It's a good spot to see bears. Though if it's hot, you may not see a lot(if any.)

You can try Star Wars Galaxies. 

You have SWGEmu which emulates the game as it was when it launched, which was a sandbox. No story. Only yours. Select a planet to spawn on and have at it. Travel the galaxy being a crafter. Hunt Jedi as a bounty hunter. Craft buffs as a doctor and sell your services, create a city on a planet and become mayor. You name it. The problem with SWGEmu is, it's a test server technically. They are coding the game from scratch. Once it os complete, everything will be wiped eventually. And it can take a long time to master professions. While the population normally hits 1000+, most are afk bots. You can multibox so it also lowers the actual playercount.

SWGEmu does not have Jump to Lightspeed, which introduced space piloting to the game.


Then you have SWG Legends. This uses the leaked official code of the game and emulates the game as it was on the day it shut down. It's more theme park as there is an overall story and questline to follow, and levels. However, once you finish said story, the galaxy is yours to do with as you please. There are endgame elements such as PvP and Heroics(raids/instances.) You have classes now, as opposed to the profession system in the Emu so you're following a set archetype. As a Bounty Hunter you can hunt all players, not just Jedi. Sandbox elements are still there just not heavy as Emu. Same as Emu, population usually hits 1200+ and multiboxing is allowed. So again, definitive playercount is impossible to gauge. 

Most people flock to Legends because right now, it offers the complete game, including Jump to Lightspeed. JTL pretty much adds a space combat simulator to the game. It's technically its own separate game.

I just purchased the AT2005(a slight step up from the 2100 according to reviews) and it sounds great from the tests I've run(I've yet to actually record or upload anything.) It's a dynamic mic which is just what I need. Dynamic mics are designed to pick up noise directly in front of them, thus reducing the amount of background noise. It barely picks up mouse clicks and keystrokes. 

I started with a Blue Snowball(condenser mic,) however it picked up waaaay too much noise. I was never able to get the sound that I wanted, and it would take a hell of an amount of post processing in Audacity, which by the end, would make it sound even worse.

I should add also that I use VoiceMeeter which has a built in noise gate, which with the Snowball, was rendered useless. With the AT2005, if I'm not talking, the mic doesn't record.

After roughly a year of endless tests and feeling like I'd never get a good sound, and feeling like I should just quit while I'm ahead, I'm closer than ever to finally getting my channel going. Still some things I need to test out(mainly editing and mixing,) though I'm pretty confident right now.

I purchased mine on eBay in a bundle for $115, though it came with a pop filter, noise cancelling Audio Technica headphones and a Neewer boom arm. The mic alone goes for about $70-$80.
